objections.claim: The no-listener executable-closure contract is internally unsatisfiable. Section 1 defines the external-tool exception as exactly three binaries (`git`, `bwrap`, and `gh`) and states that the spawn allowlist also applies to every spawned Node runtime, but the supported launcher must spawn the external `node` executable. Section 4 additionally requires doctor to establish that `sha256sum` is usable, although that executable is absent from the closed allowlist; the stated `gh` grammar also omits the `gh --version` operation doctor requires. Consequently the mandatory launcher/doctor path must either be refused by the closed grammar or execute unregistered external capabilities, so the claimed satisfiability and closed-listener-capability enforcement cannot both hold. The approach must enumerate capability-scoped exceptions and exact argument grammars for every required runtime/probe executable, including Node and any actually executed digest/version probes, with identity, environment, and listener-safety regressions.
